expect: Start from sundial reading of 13:08 (Apparent Solar Time) [1]. Apply Equation of Time: if the Sun is +10 min ahead of Mean Sun, subtract 10 min from sundial reading: 13:08 - 10 min = 12:58 Local Mean Time [1]. Apply longitude correction: 0.1° east of Greenwich = +0.4 min ≈ +0 min (negligible, accept rounding to 0) — or candidate correctly states +0.4 min giving 12:58.4 — accept 12:58 [1]. Apply BST: add 1 hour: 12:58 + 1:00 = 13:58 [1].
value: Start from sundial reading of 13:08 (Apparent Solar Time) [1]. Apply Equation of Time: if the Sun is +10 min ahead of Mean Sun, subtract 10 min from sundial reading: 13:08 - 10 min = 12:58 Local Mean Time [1]. Apply longitude correction: 0.1° east of Greenwich = −0.4 min ≈ 0 min (negligible, accept rounding to 0) — or candidate correctly states −0.4 min giving 12:57.6 — accept 12:58 [1]. Apply BST: add 1 hour: 12:58 + 1:00 = 13:58 [1].
note: F10: east of the standard meridian subtracts; the final answer 13:58 is unchanged

find: The hour lines on the dial are equally spaced in angle (15° per hour, since Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours).
replace: The shadow sweeps around the gnomon at 15° per hour, since Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours. On an equatorial dial the hour lines are equally spaced at 15°; on a horizontal dial they are not evenly spaced.

expect:
State formula: maximum altitude at transit = 90° − observer latitude + declination (for objects north of the zenith) [1 mark]. Or equivalently: altitude at transit = 90° − (latitude − declination) for Dec < latitude.
Substitute: 90° − 56° + 30° = 64° [1 mark for correct substitution, 1 mark for correct answer]. Units/statement: The galaxy is 64° above the horizon when on the meridian [1 mark].
(If student uses 90° − 56° + 30° correctly but makes an arithmetic error, 2 marks awarded for method.)
value:
State formula: maximum altitude at transit = 90° − observer latitude + declination (for objects that transit south of the zenith, that is Dec less than the latitude) [1 mark]. Or equivalently: altitude at transit = 90° − (latitude − declination) for Dec < latitude.
Substitute: 90° − 56° + 30° = 64° [1 mark for correct substitution, 1 mark for correct answer]. Units/statement: The galaxy is 64° above the horizon when on the meridian [1 mark].
(If student uses 90° − 56° + 30° correctly but makes an arithmetic error, 2 marks awarded for method.)
note: F18: the formula is for objects transiting south of the zenith
